## Independent full review — ADR-0142 (rounds 1 and 2 of 4)

An independent full review of the whole record, on the contract-review tier at effort xhigh, by a reviewer agent separate from the drafter (fed the record, the rulings and the code at `5f5f0b42` plus HotCRM at `8f52859`, never the drafter's notes), per the owner's order that spec, skills and ADR changes owe one before the seat's ACCEPT. One full review of the first substantive head, then delta reviews by the same reviewer of the commits that only apply findings, stopping at the first round with no must-fix.

| Round | Head | Verdict | must-fix / should-fix / nit | Applied in |
|:---|:---|:---|:---|:---|
| 1 (full) | `a36d060` | FAIL | 7 / 9 / 5 | `19d7532` |
| 2 (delta) | `19d7532` | FAIL | 2 / 7 / 4 | `3c6be23` |

`0ae85b0`, the PR head, merges `main` onto `a2e71ca` and leaves the record byte-identical.

### Round 1 — full review of `a36d060`

Verdict: FAIL

Reviewed: `docs/adr/0142-ownership-queue-membership-claim-and-assignment-rules.md` at `a36d060` (branch `claude/project-thread-eypatm`, committed; working tree clean; base `origin/main` `5f5f0b4221d9`; no other `docs/adr/**` file touched). HotCRM read at `8f52859`.

Summary. The shape is the right one and most of Context §1 is accurate against the code: step 3.5's arms, the hook-after-middleware ordering, `OWNER_FIELD_DEF`, the `ownership` tier table, the two reserved members and every comment the record quotes about them, the five expanders, the regime-C precedent, `updateMany`'s optionality, and HotCRM's three factories, view, rules and tests are all as described. The record fails on seven points that are not polish: it places the access path in the wrong package and omits the one gate (the `created_by` ownership floor) a queue member's write must pass; it leaves the public-form door open to a supplied `queue`; it contradicts itself on a member's insert with a queue, on a rule whose queue does not resolve, and on round-robin's degradation; it promises claim atomicity by a primitive the engine does not have and names no seam; and it silently narrows the first consumer's claimant set and strands its existing ownerless rows. Each is fixable in one round, and the fix is named below.

Gates (run from the worktree root):
- `node scripts/check-adr-symbol-anchors.mjs` — EXIT=0 (2627 anchors across 144 records resolve; the 47 `hotcrm:` anchors are reported as cross-repo and not judged — I verified each of them by hand against `8f52859`: all resolve).
- `node scripts/check-adr-links.mjs` — EXIT=0 (807 relative links resolve).
- House rules: no HTML comments; no model names; no `path:NNN` anchors; codes SCREAMING_SNAKE; proposed refusal strings carry no tracker number; type names singular, machine names snake_case, stack keys camelCase like `sharingRules`; the three Chinese rulings match their sources character for character (`.claude/skills/pm-dispatch/references/cross-repo-coordination.md` for D5, ADR-0138 Alternatives for the D1 quote, the brief's text for the D6 ruling).

---

F1 — must-fix (wrong fact + mechanism gap). The OWD owner gates are not in the security middleware, and the platform's ownership floor does not read `owner_id`.

Evidence. Context §1 says the readers of `owner_id` include "the OWD / RLS owner gates in the same middleware", D1 says `plugin-security` "consumes the contract through the kernel, as its middleware already consults the sharing service to widen an owner match", D3 injects the queue disjunct "beside the owner match in the read filter and the write gate", and the execution plan puts "the access path in `plugin-security`". In the code the middleware only stashes a depth string (`packages/plugins/plugin-security/src/security-plugin-authz-middleware.ts#registerAuthzMiddleware` step 2.6: `sc.__readScope = …` / `sc.__writeScope = …`, "so the sharing service can widen the owner-match"). The owner match itself is built in `plugin-sharing`: `packages/plugins/plugin-sharing/src/sharing-service.ts#buildReadFilter` (`ownerMatch = { owner_id: … }` OR the caller's `sys_record_share` ids, reading `__readScope`), `#buildWriteFilter`, and `#checkEdit`, whose ownership fast path `#matchesOwnerScope` "Returns `false` when the record has no owner value" — a sitting record is refused there by construction until that method learns the queue disjunct. Separately, the by-id write path carries the platform's ownership floor `owner_only_writes` / `owner_only_deletes`, `using: created_by == current_user.id` (`packages/plugins/plugin-security/src/platform-ownership-policies.ts#OWNERSHIP_FLOOR_PREDICATE`; the header calls it "a second implementation of ownership"), and the floor is dropped only when the sharing write verdict is `allow` (`packages/plugins/plugin-security/src/security-plugin-sharing-verdicts.ts#resolvePreImageFloorDrop`). So the sentence "Every reader of ownership reads `owner_id`" is false for the floor, and a queue member claiming a guest-written case (`created_by` NULL) is refused at step 2.7 unless `checkEdit` says `allow` — which it only will if the disjunct lands in `plugin-sharing`, not in the middleware.

Fix. (a) Correct Context §1: the OWD owner match lives in `plugin-sharing`'s `SharingService`; the middleware stashes depth; the platform floor reads `created_by` and is lifted by the sharing verdict. (b) In D3 name the four sites the disjunct lands in: `#buildReadFilter`'s `ownerMatch`, `#buildWriteFilter`, `#checkEdit` via `#matchesOwnerScope` (which then also lifts the floor through `#resolvePreImageFloorDrop` with no change there), and the explain engine. (c) Name where `current_user.queues` is assembled — beside the other pre-resolved sets in `packages/core/src/security/assemble-execution-context.ts` (`rlsMembership`), or say the middleware stashes it as it stashes `__readScope`. (d) Move "the access path" from `plugin-security` to `plugin-sharing` in execution plan step 1, which also removes the cross-plugin dependency merge question 2 worries about.

F2 — must-fix (broken mechanism; a hole). The guest refusal for `queue` is placed at step 3.5, which the public-form door never reaches.

Evidence. D3: "a guest never supplies it (ADR-0138 D1's branch, extended to the second anchor)". The `publicFormGrant` branch of the same middleware says "The grant bypasses every downstream write gate (FLS 2.5, owner anchor 3.5, tenant CHECK) — so the system-managed anchors must be forced HERE" and strips exactly `packages/spec/src/security/public-form.ts#PUBLIC_FORM_SERVER_MANAGED_FIELDS` (`id`, `owner_id`, `owning_business_unit_id`, `organization_id`, `tenant_id`, …), with the comment "this is the data-layer boundary that holds even if a FormView declares … one of these columns". ADR-0138 D1's "Enforced by" names both halves (the step-3.5 guest branch for endpoint doors, the `publicFormGrant` strip for form doors). The record names one. HotCRM's web-to-case is the form door; without `queue` on that list a submission could park itself in any queue.

Fix. D3 states both halves; execution plan step 1 adds `queue` to `PUBLIC_FORM_SERVER_MANAGED_FIELDS` (the list already pre-registers `owning_business_unit_id` "BEFORE it exists" for exactly this reason).

F3 — must-fix (hidden fork; the record says two incompatible things). A member's insert with a supplied `queue` cannot produce a sitting record under the record's own rules.

Evidence. D3: "on insert, a supplied `queue` is admitted when the caller holds the transfer grant or is a member of that queue (an agent logging a case straight into the intake queue)" and "`owner_id` and `queue` may be supplied together only under the transfer grant". Step 3.5's INSERT arm stamps an empty `owner_id` with the acting user (`if (userId) row.owner_id = userId`). So the agent's case lands with `owner_id` = agent and `queue` = intake — by D3's own meaning an owned record with a home queue, not a record sitting in the queue; and the agent cannot send `owner_id: null` beside `queue` without the grant. The parenthetical implies the opposite. D5 then never evaluates a rule for it (owner set).

Fix. Decide and say: either (a) the stamp is suppressed when a member supplies `queue` and no owner, so the record sits (a change to the stamp rule that must be stated as such, with the explain reason), or (b) a member's insert with `queue` is an owned record with home queue Q (today's behaviour for an agent-created case in HotCRM) and the parenthetical goes. This is a fork the maintainer should see; add it to the merge questions.

F4 — must-fix (contradiction). A rule whose queue does not resolve in the row's organization is both a 422 and a never-refused insert.

Evidence. D9: "`QUEUE_NOT_FOUND` 422, for a write or a rule naming a queue that resolves nowhere in the row's organization". D1: "A name that resolves nowhere fails closed for that reference". D5: "Intake is never refused by assignment: that is HotCRM's contract" and "A read that fails during evaluation leaves the row as it was before evaluation … and logs at `warn`". An authored `sys_queue` that exists in one organization of several is the realistic case (HotCRM's system import, the Context §2 "organization pin" row): the rule's target resolves in one organization and nowhere in the next.

Fix. Split the two: a declared rule's declared-queue target is validated at load (fail loud, as D5 already does for a `user` id); at insert, a target that resolves nowhere in the row's organization is the D5 degradation (ownerless, `queue` unset, one `warn` naming the queue and the organization); `QUEUE_NOT_FOUND` 422 stays for a caller-supplied `queue` on a write. State it in D5 and D9 in the same words.

F5 — must-fix (broken mechanism). Round-robin's degradation to least-loaded has no `load` predicate to count by.

Evidence. D5's shape: "`load?` … REQUIRED with 'least_loaded', refused otherwise". D5's round-robin bullet: "Where the driver implements no `updateMany`, round-robin degrades to least-loaded for that write and logs once at `warn`". A `round_robin` entry has no `load` by the record's own rule, so the degraded path has nothing to count — the exact "rule that silently counts everything" D5 refuses two paragraphs earlier. Merge question 7 and the Consequences repeat the degradation as if it were defined.

Fix. Degrade to park (`queue` = Q, `owner_id` empty, one `warn`), or to the next member by ordering position without a cursor (fair under no concurrency, approximate otherwise) — and say which in D5, merge question 7 and Consequences.

F6 — must-fix (broken mechanism; no seam named). The claim's one-owner guarantee rests on a conditional by-id write the engine does not have.

Evidence. D4: "The write itself is conditional on the pre-image — 'where `owner_id` is still empty' — so two members claiming at once produce exactly one owner; the loser's update matches no row and answers 409 `RESOURCE_CONFLICT`". The admission is adjudicated in the middleware; the write is the engine's by-id `update`. `packages/objectql/src/engine.ts` has no precondition / expected-version option on a by-id update (grep for `precondition`, `expectedVersion`, `ifMatch`: none on the write path); the only predicate write is the driver's optional `updateMany` (`packages/spec/src/contracts/data-driver.ts`). The record's Context §1 notes the primitive exists but D4 never says who issues it: the middleware cannot rewrite the operation into a predicate update without changing hook dispatch (`dispatch.mode` becomes `per-row`) and without colliding with the same step's rule that "a bulk change-set carrying `owner_id` fails closed"; and nothing today turns "0 rows affected" on an update by id into a 409 rather than a success envelope.

Fix. Name the seam: an engine-level precondition on the by-id update (`{ expect: { owner_id: null } }` or similar) that the gate sets and the engine lowers to the driver's conditional write, mapping 0 affected rows to `RESOURCE_CONFLICT`; state that `sys_assignment_cursor`'s version check uses the same primitive; and state what happens on a driver without `updateMany` (the record covers that for the cursor, not for the claim).

F7 — must-fix (silent drop of consumer behaviour; hidden fork). The self-claim's claimant set narrows, and HotCRM's existing ownerless backlog becomes unreachable.

Evidence. HotCRM's `createCaseSelfClaim` stamps the caller for "A write carrying a real user id … whoever they are" with edit reach — it names the admin and "the manager holding the escalation share" explicitly, and its guard 4 lets a person claim a RESOLVED unowned case by reopening it. HotCRM's `service_agent` set holds no `crm_case.allowTransfer` (`src/sales/profiles/service-agent.profile.ts`: "the agent holds no transfer grant on `crm_case`"); `system_admin` does. Under D4 the admission requires membership of the queue the pre-image's `queue` resolves to; a `service_manager` holder reaching an unowned critical case through `case_escalation_sharing` can claim it today and cannot under the record unless a member of the intake queue or a grant holder; reopening a resolved unowned case by claim has no spelling. D8's row for `case_self_claim` says only "the gate's claim admission". And every ownerless row HotCRM already holds (the triage tab is "the intake backlog") has `owner_id` NULL and no `queue`: the admission requires "its `queue` resolves to Q", so those rows cannot be claimed without the grant, and the access path (`queue IN current_user.queues`) does not show them to agents — the state HotCRM filed #1096 to end.

Fix. D8 names the narrowing as a behaviour change HotCRM accepts (and whether the escalation desk needs its own queue or a grant), names "reopen-by-claim of a resolved unowned case" as dropped, and the execution plan or the HotCRM card names the backfill (`queue` = intake where `owner_id IS NULL` on the objects a rule targets) or says legacy rows need the transfer grant. If the backfill is HotCRM's, say it is a system write of `queue` (D3 admits it as the platform).

---

F8 — should-fix. A reader that special-cases `queue` is missing from D6's re-admission list.

Evidence. `packages/lint/src/validate-approval-approvers.ts`: the `APPROVAL_APPROVER_TYPE_UNSUPPORTED` finding keys on `APPROVER_VALUE_BINDINGS[...].source === 'unsupported'` with the hint "Queue approvers need a real ownership-queue implementation before they take effect."; `GROUP_ROUTED_TYPES` is `position`, `team`, `department` and its header excludes "the opaque `queue`" from `approval-approvers-may-resolve-empty`. Once a queue is a group whose membership is runtime data, it belongs in `GROUP_ROUTED_TYPES` (or the node's empty-slate lint is blind to a queue-only step), and the hint is dead text. D5 cites that very lint as the model for the assignment rule's authoring-time check, so the omission is in the record's own frame.

Fix. D6 gains item: `validate-approval-approvers.ts` adds `queue` to `GROUP_ROUTED_TYPES` and retires the unsupported hint; the `APPROVAL_APPROVER_TYPE_UNSUPPORTED` arm stops firing by construction once the binding changes.

F9 — should-fix. D6 item 2 contradicts itself on the empty queue.

Evidence. "an empty expansion takes the path the graph types already take (the 'expanded to nobody' warning, then the node's `onEmptyApprovers`)" and, in the same item, "The `queue:ID` literal slot is never written again". The graph path (`packages/plugins/plugin-approvals/src/approval-service.ts#resolveApproverSpec`, types in `GRAPH_APPROVER_TYPES`: `team`, `department`, `business_unit`, `bu`, `position`, `org_membership_level`) warns and then `return [`${type}:${a.value}`]` — it writes the literal slot. The `return []` path is `PERSON_APPROVER_TYPES` (`manager`, `field`).

Fix. "warn as the graph types do, then return `[]` as the person types do" — a new combination, stated as such.

F10 — should-fix. D5's organization pin names the wrong deriver for most writes.

Evidence. D5: "pinned to the row's organization as `resolveSystemInsertOrganization` derives it (ADR-0131 D9)". `packages/objectql/src/engine.ts#resolveSystemInsertOrganization` returns `undefined` when the context carries `tenantId` or every row names its organization; it derives only for an organization-less system write. The guest door's organization is the door's binding (ADR-0138 D4 item 4); a system import naming `organization_id` per row carries it on the row. Context §1 states this correctly; D5 does not.

Fix. "the row's organization — the context's `tenantId`, the row's own column, or the one `resolveSystemInsertOrganization` derives when neither names one".

F11 — should-fix. Context §3 contradicts D8 and the execution plan on what HotCRM deletes.

Evidence. Context §3: "HotCRM deletes 587 lines plus a hook, a sharing rule and four tests". 587 lines is the whole of `_case-assignment.ts`, which D8 and execution plan step 2 keep one third of (`createCaseEscalationReassign`). Of the four pins Context §2 names, `test/case-assignment.test.ts` and `test/flow-sla-ownerless-assignment.test.ts` drive the escalation hand-off that stays, and `test/ownership-model.test.ts` pins the transfer-grant roster and door ① for `lead_auto_assign`, most of which stays. References says "the five tests named in Context §2".

Fix. "two of the three factories, `lead_auto_assign`, the triage rule, `claim-case-one-owner-writer.test.ts`, and the covered cases of the other pins".

F12 — should-fix. Least-loaded under concurrent or batch inserts is not walked.

Evidence. D5 gives round-robin a cursor and a retry; for `least_loaded` it says nothing about two inserts (or N rows of one batch) that each count before any is written and all choose the same member. HotCRM's hook has the same property, so this is not a regression, but the brief's walk asks for it and the record claims "the race is settled by the write" only for the claim.

Fix. One sentence in D5: least-loaded is approximate under concurrency and within a batch (as HotCRM's is today), or the batch adjusts counts locally per row.

F13 — should-fix (hidden fork). The injected column is named with a plain business word and the collision rule is unstated.

Evidence. `packages/objectql/src/registry.ts#applySystemFields` injects `owner_id` only when the schema declares none (`if (wantOwner && !schema.fields?.owner_id)`). D3 injects `queue` "on exactly the objects it injects `owner_id` on". `queue` already names a column (`packages/platform-objects/src/audit/sys-job-queue.object.ts`) and config keys (`packages/spec/src/system/worker.zod.ts`) — on ineligible objects today, but an app's `ownership: 'user'` object with its own `queue` picklist is ordinary business modelling. Skipping injection would leave the anchor silently absent (ADR-0078); overriding would break the author's field.

Fix. D9 states the rule — recommend refusing at registration with a prescription, as HotCRM's rule 10 does for a declared `organization_id` — or names the column with a suffix (`queue_name`) and says why not.

F14 — should-fix (ADR-0078). A stack that declares `queues` / `assignmentRules` in a composition with no queue service is silently inert.

Evidence. D1: "when no queue service is registered, no queue exists, and every queue-dependent admission below fails closed". That covers the gate; nothing covers a declared `assignment_rule` whose evaluator never runs, or a declared `queue` nothing resolves — a Zod-valid instance that does nothing, the state ADR-0078 forbids. Also unstated: the `sys_metadata_activation` types `queue` and `assignment_rule` (its `type` column lists the registry types in its description; `plugin-sharing` spells `SHARING_RULE_ACTIVATION_TYPE` for its own) and the lint completeness row.

Fix. D1 or D5: a stack declaring either key in a composition that registers no queue service is refused at boot (or warned once, loudly, by name); execution plan step 1 names the two activation types.

F15 — should-fix. A member losing membership while holding records is not stated.

Evidence. The brief's walk; D3 says a set `queue` on an owned record "confers no access", which implies the answer, but D4's release admits "the pre-image's `owner_id` is the caller and `queue` is unchanged" without saying whether a non-member may release to a queue they no longer belong to.

Fix. One sentence: ownership is not membership — the owner keeps the record; release back to the home queue is admitted for the owner whether or not still a member (recommended, since the record then becomes visible to the queue's members), or refused — pick one.

F16 — should-fix. D7's wording and reader list.

Evidence. D7 item 2: "the runtime union is then 'the authorable enum plus `field`'s per-record arm'" — `field` is already in `ShareRecipientType`; after re-admission the two lists are the same seven members, and `packages/spec/src/contracts/sharing-service.test.ts` (which today pins "the stored-row union is exactly the authoring enum plus the reserved `queue`", with an `@ts-expect-error` on `queue`) flips to equality. Two readers D7 does not list: `packages/plugins/plugin-sharing/src/objects/sys-sharing-rule.object.ts#SysSharingRule` — `recipient_type` is a `Field.select` whose options comment says "`queue` was removed" and which `field-recipient.test.ts` holds equal to `ShareRecipientType`; and the `SharingLevel` comment in `packages/spec/src/security/sharing.zod.ts` ("the same reason `ShareRecipientType` below dropped `queue` / `guest`").

Fix. Rephrase item 2 as equality; add the select options and the two comments to item 5.

---

N1 — nit. Context §1: "`transfer` is a member … of the grant bits (`packages/core/src/security/effective-object-permissions.ts#GRANT_BITS`)" — the bit is `allowTransfer`; `transfer` is the verb `checkObjectPermission` maps onto it.

N2 — nit. D1: "a registry entry beside `position` and `sharing_rule`, `allowRuntimeCreate: false`" — `position`'s entry in `packages/spec/src/kernel/metadata-plugin.zod.ts#DEFAULT_METADATA_TYPE_REGISTRY` is `allowRuntimeCreate: true`; only `sharing_rule` is the model.

N3 — nit. Context §1 cites "ADR-0052 §5" for the polymorphic pointer shape; §5 of ADR-0052 is the ActivityPointer model (a structured pointer on `sys_activity`); the `referenceVia` key itself was ruled on objectui#12489 (`6203737086`), per `packages/spec/src/data/field.zod.ts`. Cite both or the field schema alone.

N4 — nit. Verification notes refer to "the brief's citation" and to "the repository's 14 open pull requests at drafting time"; a PR reader cannot see the brief and the count is ephemeral. Cite the card comment, drop the count.

N5 — nit. D4's admission says "the write is single-record (`single`; …)" — `single` is a local in the middleware (`const single = !Array.isArray(opCtx.data)`), not a named symbol; spell the condition out.

---

What I checked and found correct (so the fix round need not re-verify): step 3.5's INSERT/UPDATE/guest/delegation/referential-clear arms and its "runs inside the engine's operation, after this middleware" sentence; `permission.zod.ts#ObjectPermissionSchema` `allowTransfer` text; `explain.zod.ts#ExplainOperationSchema`; `engine-middleware-operation-vocabulary.test.ts#DESTRUCTIVE_LIFECYCLE_VERBS` (`purge`, `transfer`, `restore`); the explain engine's transfer-as-update deferral; `OWNER_FIELD_DEF`; the `applySystemFields` tier table; `ObjectAccessScopeSchema`; `recipient-resolver.ts#DEFAULT_OWNER_FIELDS` and the `user:`/`role:`/`team:`/`owner_of:` grammar; `claimSeedOwnership`'s NULL arm since #23354; the insert order (middleware → `applyFieldDefaults` → `beforeInsert` per row → `resolveSystemInsertOrganization` → write → `afterInsert`); `HookContextSchema` fields and `HookSchema.runAs`; every `queue` item in `approval.zod.ts`, `approval-service.ts#resolveApproverSpec`, `sharing.zod.ts`, `contracts/sharing-service.ts`, `sharing-rule-service.ts#expandRecipient` / `#warnOnEmptyUnitExpansion`, `bu-tree-recompute.ts#BU_TREE_RECIPIENT_TYPES`, `recipient-membership-recompute.ts#RECIPIENT_MEMBERSHIP_SOURCES`, `validate-org-axis-red-lines.ts`, migration 17, the dogfood `sharing-rules` row and `access-level.ts`; `PositionGraphService` / `TeamGraphService` / `BusinessUnitGraphService` and `expandPositionUsers`'s "deliberately NOT identical"; the four membership objects; `sharing_rule`'s registry entry; `declared-sharing-rules.ts`, `SysSharingRule`, `compileCelToFilter`, `PositionSchema`; `updateMany` across the five drivers (`SqliteWasmDriver extends SqlDriver`); `PermissionDeniedError` 403; `RESOURCE_CONFLICT` in the standard catalog; the job-queue capability and `sys_job_queue`; ADR numbering (`0136`, `0140` absent, `0141` newest) and the 0019 collision; and in HotCRM: the three factories' triggers, priorities, `runAs`, pools, load predicates, organization pin, guard order, `CLAIMABLE_TARGET_STATUSES`, the triage view's filters, the four sharing rules, the claim flow and action, `lead_auto_assign`, the `lead_assignment` header, `setup.mdx`, `AGENTS.md` rules 1–2, 9, 10, the SLA sweep's `status: 'escalated'` transition, and the five tests.

Consistency with accepted records: no silent contradiction found of ADR-0049, 0056 D3, 0057 D1/D3/D5, 0058 D1–D3, 0073 D2/D3, 0077, 0078 (except F14's gap), 0086 D1, 0087 D2, 0090 D3/D8/D10, 0105 D9, 0111 D3/D7, 0112 D1/D3, 0117 D1/D4, 0118 D2/D3, 0131 D1–D4/D6/D9 or 0138 D1/D4. The quoted D1 text of ADR-0138 is verbatim. The regime-C characterisation matches the 2026-10-19 note in ADR-0131 D6.

### Round 2 — delta review of `19d7532`

Verdict: FAIL

Reviewed: `docs/adr/0142-ownership-queue-membership-claim-and-assignment-rules.md` at `19d7532` (branch `claude/project-thread-eypatm`, committed; working tree clean; delta from `a36d060` is 209 insertions / 108 deletions in the one file). Code read at `origin/main` `5f5f0b4221d9`; HotCRM at `8f52859`.

Summary. Every round-1 finding is closed or honestly carried (closure table below), and the rewritten Context §1 is now accurate against `plugin-sharing` and the `created_by` floor to the sentence. The delta fails on two points that the new mechanisms introduced rather than inherited, both one-paragraph fixes: the named landing site for the access path (`matchesOwnerScope`) is the fast path shared with `checkDelete`, so the disjunct as placed confers the delete the same paragraph says is never conferred; and the new claimant rule's "nobody else does" misses two arms the two by-id write gates actually admit, one of which lets a disowned record's creator re-own it without the transfer grant. Seven should-fix items follow, mostly places where a new mechanism needs its owner or its missing artefact named.

Gates (worktree root, at `19d7532`):
- `node scripts/check-adr-symbol-anchors.mjs` — EXIT=0 (2648 anchors across 144 records resolve; the record's 14 `hotcrm:` anchors are reported as cross-repo, not judged; I re-checked the ones the delta touched against `8f52859`: all resolve). The new in-repo anchors (`rls-membership-resolver.ts#IRlsMembershipResolver`, `platform-ownership-policies.ts#OWNERSHIP_FLOOR_PREDICATE`, `security-plugin-sharing-verdicts.ts#resolvePreImageFloorDrop`, the four `sharing-service.ts` symbols, `public-form.ts#PUBLIC_FORM_SERVER_MANAGED_FIELDS`) all resolve to the symbols the text describes.
- `node scripts/check-adr-links.mjs` — EXIT=0 (807 relative links resolve).
- House rules: no HTML comments, no model names, no `path:NNN` anchors, codes SCREAMING_SNAKE, proposed runtime strings carry no tracker number, Chinese rulings unchanged from `a36d060`.

---

Closure of round 1

- F1 (owner match in `plugin-sharing`; `created_by` floor) — closed. Context §1, TL;DR 2, D1 placement, D3 "Who sees it" and execution plan step 1 all moved; the text now matches `buildReadFilter` / `buildWriteFilter` / `checkEdit` / `matchesOwnerScope`, step 2.6's stash, `OWNERSHIP_FLOOR_PREDICATE` and `resolvePreImageFloorDrop` as they stand. See R2-F1 for the one site it names wrongly.
- F2 (public-form door) — closed. D3 names both halves; plan step 1 adds `queue` to `PUBLIC_FORM_SERVER_MANAGED_FIELDS`.
